votes.motion: Approve the work session minutes of February 20, 2024, April 16, 2024, May 14, 2024 and May 21, 2024.
votes.description: The Council approved the minutes from four prior work session meetings as part of the opening ceremony.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 56 of 2024 (Zoning Incentives for Adaptive Reuse and Preservation of Buildings Text Amendment).
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted an ordinance amending Title 21A of the Salt Lake City Code to remove zoning barriers and provide incentives for adaptive reuse and preservation of buildings citywide.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and adopt Ordinance 57 of 2024 (Zoning Map Amendment at 1544 and 1550 South 900 West).
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and adopted an ordinance rezoning two parcels at approximately 1544 and 1550 South 900 West from R-1/7,000 to RMF-30 to allow low-density multi-family residential development such as townhomes.

votes.motion: Close the public hearing and affirm adoption of Ordinance 53 of 2024, confirming the compensation adjustment for executive municipal officers.
votes.description: The Council closed the public hearing and affirmed an ordinance confirming compensation adjustments for executive municipal officers of Salt Lake City Corporation, consistent with recent changes to Utah State Code 10-3-818.

votes.motion: Adopt Resolution 19 of 2024 for the next round of Public Utilities Bonds, and refer to the consent agenda to set the date for a public hearing on August 13, 2024.
votes.description: The Council adopted a resolution authorizing the issuance and sale of up to $39,525,000 in Public Utilities revenue bonds (Series 2024A) for water infrastructure improvements and set a public hearing date of August 13, 2024.

The Council approved all items on the consent agenda, including setting a public hearing date for Public Utilities Revenue Bonds and SECC Text Amendment, an MU-8 Zone ordinance clarification, and three board appointments (Steve Bloch and Michael Dodd to the PNUT Advisory Board, and Emily Khan to the Human Rights Commission).
